Problem: How many terms will there be if the expression \(\left(4 x^{3} + x^{-3} + 2\right)^{2016}\) is expanded and like terms are combined?

<reflection>
The expression is a trinomial raised to the 2016th power. Multinomial expansion gives terms of the form \binom{2016}{a,b,c}(4x^3)^a(x^{-3})^b2^c with a+b+c=2016 and a,b,c\ge0. The exponent of x in such a term is 3a-3b=3(a-b). Let k=a-b; then the exponent is 3k. From a=k+b and c=2016-k-2b, nonnegativity requires k\ge -b and k\le 2016-2b. Since b\ge0, k\le 2016, and the maximum k is 2016, attained when b=0, a=2016, c=0.
The assumption k≥0 is unjustified and false when considering the full range of k. In fact k can be negative, which allows b to be larger than 1008, up to b=2016 with a=c=0.
Determine the full feasible range of k by analyzing the constraints on b without assuming k≥0; show that k can be any integer from -2016 to 2016.
</reflection>
